questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My study destination was rated really high for forestry schools, so the quality of teaching. Also I wanted to gain experience from north /boreal forests, supporting my academic knowledge. I also wanted to go somewhere more remote, where student community is strong.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My experience was near to perfect. The quality of courses and teaching were great! Everyone spoke really good english. All practicalities considering the exchange worked out well.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was really easy, we got information through email but also a lot of important information could be found from school's webpage.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I arrived for the orientation week, so all the assistance that I received was happening during that time. I felt like it was enough.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Orientation week was from the most part remote in Zoom. I would have liked to have more of the days already at the university, to get to know the place and the people sooner.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was rather easy to find housing for me. I made a post of myself in multiple Facebook groups for renting a room. Useful Facebook groups:  Lägenheter i Umeå. Studentbostad i Umeå. I sayed in an apartment rented by a girl who was doing her exchange that semester. Of course when you apply housing on your own you have to be careful to avoid being scammed.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Umeå is an easy city to get by with a bike or bus!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think it's great that exchange students were helped out with getting housing. But when I saw my exchange friends living in student housing, they were not in good condition and dirty. Also the roof was looking like there was mold.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was rather easy after all (even though everything is confusing in the beginning), and the Mobility Team was helpful and responded quickly to all the questions considering registration.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registration could be done in Ladok one week before the course started or on the first day in class (if I remember correctly).

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: If I had questions, the course leaders and the Mobility Team were responding to emails in short notice.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was actually very successful. First I did not got in my first priority course. I was asking help from the Mobility Team and they quided me to ask from the course leader after the first day if anyone had cancelled their registration. So I did and ended up getting a place from the course I wanted! So that was really great. Also I wanted to change my second course as well, and that was not an issue.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Registration process is not hard. If you don't get your first priority course and you really want it, be brave to ask if there is any possibility to get in if someone cancelles. Also, if you notice during the exchange that you might want to change the second period course, that was not a hard process if you have a pre-approval for it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Teachers were great, friendly and respectful. The course contents were quite broad, yet they concentrated mostly on Swedish / boreal forest perspective, so it was not very international scale on that matter.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses was very fine. I think it was a great balance of learning but not over doing or burning out. Some of people might find the level too easy, but I think it was fine.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Since I'm not danish and I come from a northern country, I'm maybe more used to the style in Sweden compared to UCPH. And I do prefer that a lot more compared to UCPH. I have never done an oral exam before coming to Denmark, so the examinations can be really challenging or even awfull situations. Also, I think the teaching is more distant and hierarcical in UCPH than in SLU. Teachers in UCPH might "target" you and pressure a lot more than in SLU. So if you want softer way of teaching, then Sweden might be a good choise.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: 1) Forest History - Human utilisation and vegetation dynamics 2) Forest Ecosystem Ecology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Forest History - Human utilisation and vegetation dynamics. The professor Lars Östlund is probably one of the best teachers I have ever had. He has a lot of knowledge and passion for his work, yet he is a very kind person. The course consists a very nice field week in the north of Sweden. Also other great fieldwork days near to campuss. You learn a lot of forest history subjects. The course contents are important to understand when studying forest and nature management.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Wifi for the apartment. Bike and fixing the bike (roads are not great). Buying a lock for your locker in university.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Movie tickets and some of the groceries.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Thursday soup in skogis pub for example.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a university gym in the basement, which is free for the students to use. It was small, but very nice to have. Also a ping pong table inside the university was very nice.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Thursday pub and soup is a very nice event where you can eat and socialize.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: To go to the sauna by the river and go in the nature (there is a lot of beautiful forests, mire, nydala lake...).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, people are nice and friendly. However, I speak swedish so it was easier for me to communicate with the locals. Also I share more or less the same culture so it was easier. But it's not easy to make friends with the locals, like with the other internationals.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: They like to talk english and are very appreciative if you try to speak swedish, so just be brave and try! Also, if you go to the university pub and other events of school, people are more relaxed to talk there.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Kindness and happiness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be brave to talk some swedish, join the social events like the Thursday pub and the student union groups /events (we did a weekend hike with the student union hiking group).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be ready to buy or rent a bike.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The fieldweek in the north.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Enhancing my swedish skills and being brave to speak swedish.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I can only recommend to go for an exchange to SLU Umeå campus!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
